name: The French Crown: From Charlemagne to Napoleon
description: A thousand years of French kings: Frankish warlords, Capetian builders, a war with England, voyages to Canada, the Sun King and the fall of the monarchy.

checkpoints.name: The Frankish kings
checkpoints.note: Charles Martel strengthened Frankish power as mayor of the palace. His grandson Charlemagne was crowned emperor in 800 and ruled much of western Europe. The Carolingian dynasty's line of kings in the western lands ended in 987.

checkpoints.name: The Capetians
checkpoints.note: From 987 the Kingdom of France was ruled by the Capetian line, who slowly built royal power around Paris. Eleanor of Aquitaine married King Louis VII in 1137; after their marriage ended in 1152 she married Henry of Anjou, soon king of England.

checkpoints.name: War with England
checkpoints.note: The Hundred Years' War set the French crown against English kings who claimed it. Joan of Arc, a young woman from the east of France, helped turn the war and was executed in 1431; by 1453 the French king held nearly all the land.

checkpoints.name: Voyages and the Sun King
checkpoints.note: Jacques Cartier sailed to the St. Lawrence in 1534 for the French crown, the start of New France, and Samuel de Champlain founded Quebec in 1608. Henry IV ended the wars of religion with the Edict of Nantes in 1598, and Louis XIV, king for over seventy years, built the Palace of Versailles.

checkpoints.name: Revolution and empire
checkpoints.note: Louis XVI's government sank into debt and crisis, and on 14 July 1789 Parisians stormed the Bastille. The French Revolution ended the monarchy, Louis was executed in 1793, and after the revolutionary wars Napoleon crowned himself emperor in 1804 to head the First French Empire.
